item.research_question: Can rare-earth-free high magnetic anisotropy be achieved in single-phase high entropy alloy thin films using rapid thermal annealing, and how does the addition of Platinum influence phase ordering and coercivity?
item.material_system: FeCoNiMnCu (equiatomic precursor) and (FeCoNiMnCu)Pt (50 at.% Pt addition)
item.processing_route: Direct-current magnetron sputtering onto thermally oxidized Si/SiO2 substrates at room temperature or elevated temperatures (20–700 °C), followed by rapid thermal annealing (RTA) at 600 °C for 10–60 seconds in vacuum
item.test_conditions: Magnetic properties measured via VSM and SQUID; structural analysis via GIXRD, θ-2θ XRD, HAADF-STEM, and SAED; First-Order Reversal Curve (FORC) analysis in in-plane and out-of-plane geometries
key_findings: As-grown FeCoNiMnCu films exhibit a coercivity of 10 Oe, which increases to 390 Oe after 30 s of RTA at 600 °C (approx. 40-fold increase).
Inclusion of 50 at.% Pt leads to a single L10 high entropy intermetallic phase after 60 s of RTA at 600 °C.
The (FeCoNiMnCu)Pt L10 phase shows a coercivity increase of 3 orders of magnitude, reaching 2.50 kOe (in-plane) and 1.46 kOe (out-of-plane).
The L10 order parameter (S) extracted from XRD intensities is 0.8, indicating significant chemical ordering.
Saturation magnetization (Ms) for FeCoNiMnCu films is 595 ± 45 emu cm−3 (as-grown) and 590 ± 30 emu cm−3 (after RTA).
The effective uniaxial anisotropy constant (Ku) for the Pt-based L10 film is 2 × 10^6 erg cm−3.
RTA induces void formation in 13 nm films after 30 s, covering 45% area fraction, while 50 nm films show <5% area fraction.
DFT calculations suggest Mn-Mn magnetic ordering is ferromagnetic for Mn:Cu ratios ≤ 0.25 and antiferromagnetic for ratios > 0.25.
item.mechanism: The authors propose that RTA induces microstructural changes, anisotropic strain, and directional chemical order that strengthen domain wall pinning in FeCoNiMnCu films. For the Pt-containing films, the reduction of cubic symmetry to a tetragonal L10 structure combined with strong spin-orbit coupling from Pt provides the intrinsic magnetocrystalline anisotropy, while bimodal coercivity arises from a two-step reversal process involving large (001)-textured grains and smaller randomly oriented grains.
item.limitations: The authors note that the extracted Ku is not representative of the intrinsic magnetocrystalline anisotropy due to the polycrystalline microstructure and is lower than binary L10 FePt and CoPt alloys. Additionally, the saturation magnetization is reduced compared to bulk FePt and CoPt values.
item.future_work: The authors suggest that coercivity could be enhanced through microstructural optimization, specifically by reducing grain size, which may be achieved by adjusting the RTA time and temperature.
quotes: Inclusion of 50 at.% Pt in the film leads to ordering of a single L10 high entropy intermetallic phase after RTA, along with high magnetic anisotropy and 3 orders of magnitude coercivity increase.
The L10 order parameter can be extracted from the ratio of integrated intensities of the superlattice and fundamental peaks according to S=I001/I002exp.I001/I002calc.
We propose that these high Hc FORC features are associated with small and randomly oriented grains, which are evident by the observation of L10 peaks in GIXRD.
